analysis.evidence: אֶת־שְׁמוֹ marks “his name” as the direct object, and נֹחַ supplies the name given.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third masculine singular, with prefixed conjunction וַ־.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּקְרָא אֶת שְׁמוֹ נֹחַ, אֶת marks שְׁמוֹ (“his name”) as the direct object of וַיִּקְרָא (“he called”). The possessive suffix makes שְׁמוֹ definite, and נֹחַ supplies the name given.
analysis.morphology: Unsuffixed direct-object particle with no prefix.

draft.change: Add Genesis 5:29 as an example of giving a child a name under the existing Hebrew noun sense.
draft.definition: The personal name by which someone is known.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:29 places the child's given name, נֹחַ, immediately after שְׁמוֹ, “his name.”

patch.value: Lamech calls his son Noah. The child's given name follows שְׁמוֹ, “his name.”

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּקְרָא אֶת שְׁמוֹ נֹחַ, “he called his name Noah,” אֶת marks שְׁמוֹ as the object of וַיִּקְרָא. The following word נֹחַ supplies the name given to the child.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with the third-person masculine singular possessive suffix ־וֹ, referring to the child.
analysis.sense: name by which someone is known

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for נֹחַ linked to the root article nuach.
draft.definition: Noah, the son whom Lamech names in hope of relief from toil.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:29 gives the name נֹחַ and explains it through the wordplay on יְנַחֲמֵנוּ, “he will comfort us.”

analysis.evidence: וַיִּקְרָא אֶת־שְׁמוֹ נֹחַ means “he called his name Noah.” Lamech explains his choice with יְנַחֲמֵנוּ, “he will comfort us,” expressing hope for relief from toil on the cursed ground. The verb נחם echoes the sound of the name, which is associated with נוח, “rest.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: After וַיִּקְרָא אֶת שְׁמוֹ נֹחַ (“he named him Noah”), לֵאמֹר introduces the father’s words explaining the name. The quotation begins זֶה יְנַחֲמֵנוּ (“this one will comfort us”).
analysis.morphology: Qal infinitive construct with prefixed preposition לְ.

draft.change: Clarify the use of prefixed לְ in the Genesis 2:23 evidence for the existing “this-one” sense of זֶה.
draft.definition: Used independently, the feminine singular זֹאת can point to a woman present as “this one.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 2:23 places לְזֹאת before יִקָּרֵא אִשָּׁה, identifying the woman who receives the designation.

analysis.evidence: After naming the child נֹחַ, his father says זֶה יְנַחֲמֵנוּ, “this one will comfort us.” זֶה points to Noah as the one who will bring comfort.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular demonstrative pronoun, used independently as the subject of יְנַחֲמֵנוּ.
analysis.sense: Points to a person present as “this one.”

analysis.evidence: זֶה, “this one,” refers to the newborn Noah. The suffix ־נוּ means “us,” and מִמַּעֲשֵׂנוּ וּמֵעִצְּבוֹן יָדֵינוּ identifies the work and painful toil from which Lamech expects comfort.
analysis.morphology: Piel imperfect, third person masculine singular, with a first person common plural object suffix.

analysis.evidence: Lamech pairs מִמַּעֲשֵׂנוּ with וּמֵעִצְּבוֹן יָדֵינוּ, “and from the toil of our hands.” The reference to the ground that YHWH cursed identifies the work as the labor of cultivating it.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with prefixed מִן (its נ assimilates to the following מ) and first-person common plural possessive suffix ־נוּ.

analysis.evidence: יָדֵינוּ completes the construct phrase ‘the painful toil of our hands’. Its parallel, מִמַּעֲשֵׂנוּ ‘from our work’, and the reference to the ground that YHWH cursed identify the toil as the hardship of working the soil.
analysis.gloss: and from the painful toil of
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with prefixed וּ־ ‘and’ and מֵ־ ‘from’.

analysis.evidence: In מִן הָאֲדָמָה, “from the ground,” the ground that YHWH cursed is the source of the painful toil described as עִצְּבוֹן יָדֵינוּ, “the toil of our hands.”
analysis.sense: out of, made from; from (a source or giver)

analysis.evidence: מִן הָאֲדָמָה identifies the ground as the source of the toil of their hands. The relative clause אֲשֶׁר אֵרְרָהּ יַהְוֶה identifies it as the ground YHWH cursed, linking the toil to working the soil.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute common noun with the prefixed definite article הָ־.
analysis.sense: the ground that is tilled; soil

analysis.evidence: אֲשֶׁר introduces the clause modifying הָאֲדָמָה, “the ground which Yahweh cursed.” The feminine singular object suffix ־הּ on אֵרְרָהּ refers back to הָאֲדָמָה.
analysis.morphology: Invariable relative particle without prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Broaden the proposed Qal definition to include a curse pronounced on a thing, and cite the feminine participle applied to the ground.
draft.definition: To pronounce a curse on someone or something. The passive participle describes whoever or whatever is under the curse.
draft.evidence: In Gen.3.17 Yahweh addresses Adam, but the subject of אֲרוּרָה is הָאֲדָמָה, the ground. In Gen.3.14 the corresponding masculine form אָרוּר describes the serpent.

article.summary: אָרַר means to pronounce a curse on someone or something. In Genesis 3 Yahweh uses the passive participle when he declares first the serpent and then the ground cursed.

senses.definition: To pronounce a curse on someone or something. The passive participle describes whoever or whatever is under the curse.

evidence.note: Yahweh addresses the serpent directly with אָרוּר אַתָּה, “cursed are you.”
In אֲרוּרָה הָאֲדָמָה, “cursed is the ground,” the feminine participle agrees with the ground. Adam will eat from it in toil all his life.

analysis.evidence: In הָאֲדָמָה אֲשֶׁר אֵרְרָהּ יַהְוֶה, “the ground that Yahweh had cursed,” יַהְוֶה is the subject. The object suffix ־הּ refers back to הָאֲדָמָה, the ground pronounced cursed in Genesis 3:17.
analysis.morphology: Piel perfect, third-person masculine singular, with a third-person feminine singular object suffix.
analysis.sense: To pronounce a curse on someone or something.

analysis.evidence: In אֲשֶׁר אֵרְרָהּ יַהְוֶה, “which Yahweh cursed,” יַהְוֶה names the subject of אֵרְרָהּ. The feminine singular object suffix refers back to הָאֲדָמָה, “the ground.”
analysis.morphology: Proper noun, masculine singular, without prefix or suffix
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel
